meta.description: A live radio app for an Egyptian broadcaster: listeners tune in, chat in real time behind a profanity filter and book their own on-air slot once a moderator approves it.

caseStudy.title: Hanze3
caseStudy.lead: A live radio app for an Egyptian broadcaster: listeners tune in, chat in real time behind a profanity filter and book their own on-air slot once a moderator approves it.

brief.title: The brief
text: The broadcaster wanted listeners to do more than listen: talk to each other while the show is on, and even get on air themselves.
And the stream had to be cheap to run, without a dedicated streaming server.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Built the native Android app in Java with XML layouts.
Played the programme from audio files in Firebase Storage, loaded into the player by link, so no streaming server was needed.
Built the live chat on Firebase, with a profanity filter I wrote that replaces offensive words with asterisks.
Built the admin panel: approve talk show requests and delete offensive messages.
Let admins publish the weekly programme by date and time slot and show when a talk show is on air.

items.title: Tune in
items.text: The current programme plays from Firebase Storage, with no streaming server to pay for.

items.title: Talk while it's on
items.text: Listeners chat in real time; insults turn into asterisks before anyone sees them.

items.title: Book a talk show slot
items.text: Listeners request a slot of up to 30 minutes, and a moderator approves it.

items.title: Run the station
items.text: Approve requests, delete messages and publish the week's schedule.

team.title: Team
team.text: I built the app myself, working directly with the client.

outcome.title: The result
outcome.text: A low-cost live radio app with listener chat, moderated on-air slots and a weekly schedule the station runs itself.
